question: After the `stale_run` consumer bug is fixed and real behavior proof is posted, should maintainers keep this Track B branch stacked behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101910 for review, or wait for Track A to land and require a fresh branch from main?
rationale: The patch depends on Track A primitives and changes default liveness/message-delivery behavior, so a human owner must decide the merge sequencing and acceptable proof threshold.

options.title: Keep stacked after fixes
options.body: Fix the `stale_run` consumer path, add Track B live proof, and keep the branch stacked until Track A is ready to merge.

options.title: Wait for Track A on main
options.body: Pause this branch until Track A lands, then ask for a clean rebased PR from main with the same Track B changes.

options.title: Narrow the stale-steer scope
options.body: Land only the fake-heartbeat and attribution fixes now, and defer stale steer capture until the active-wake/drop behavior is redesigned.

recommendation.title: Keep stacked after fixes
recommendation.body: Fix the `stale_run` consumer path, add Track B live proof, and keep the branch stacked until Track A is ready to merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the canonical Track B design comment and the stacked Track A branch that this PR builds on.
